topic: The Mathematical Trinity: Powers, Roots, and Logarithms

sections.title: The Foundation: Exponential Growth (1 min)
sections.content: Introduce the base and exponent as a 'growth engine'. Visualize a tree growing: a seed (base 2) branching into 2^x. This sets the prerequisite for understanding powers as repeated multiplication.
sections.example: A rabbit population doubles every month: 2^1=2, 2^2=4, 2^3=8. The exponent 3 represents the time passed.

sections.title: The Inverse Shift: Roots (1.5 min)
sections.content: Transition from growth to finding the 'origin'. If we know the result (the grown tree), how do we find the base? Introduce radical notation as the 'undoing' of exponents.
sections.example: If a square garden has an area (result) of 16m², we use the square root (√16) to find the side length (base 4). Visualize a square collapsing back into a single side.

sections.title: The Time Seeker: Logarithms (1.5 min)
sections.content: Introduce logarithms as the method to find the 'missing time' (the exponent). If we know the growth rate and the result, the log tells us how long it took to get there. Use a timeline visual.
sections.example: The rabbit population is now 32. If they double (base 2) every month, how many months (x) passed? Log2(32) = 5. The log reveals the 'hidden' time elapsed.

sections.title: Synthesizing the Trinity (1 min)
sections.content: Conclude by unifying the three: Power = Base^Exponent; Root = Result^(1/exponent); Log = Exponent of the Base. Show a circular graphic where arrows rotate between these three states.
sections.example: Equation map: 2^3 = 8 (Power) | 3√8 = 2 (Root) | log2(8) = 3 (Log). A single relationship, three different perspectives.
